A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ND-SDF research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantitative and qualitative reconstruction experiments on four datasets, plus component, prior-model, warm-up, and rendering ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, convergence diagnostics, confidence-map comparisons, and experiments with deliberately biased normal priors.

M1.justification: The deflection network, adaptive losses, angle-guided sampling and rendering, and warm-up procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. Equation 3 corrects the expansion of the already specified Laplace-CDF mapping; it does not establish a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate indoor reconstruction on ScanNet, Replica, Tanks and Temples, and ScanNet++. Appendix B.4 in v3 adds a distinct input condition: deliberately corrupted normal priors in smooth regions of one existing ScanNet++ scene. No new dataset or application domain is added.

E2.justification: DebSDF, already included in v2's ScanNet table, is added to the Tanks and Temples, ScanNet++, and Replica comparisons. It replaces MonoSDF in Figure 4 and NeuRIS in the Tanks and Temples qualitative comparison. New Figure 12 also compares NCC, edge, and uncertainty maps against the proposed angle map, substantially expanding the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: The new robustness experiment uses SAM-selected smooth regions and normal rotations of 0, 5, 15, 30, 45, and 60 degrees; comparator results are reported only at the endpoints. Figure 11 adds a rendering-weight analysis across inverse-variance settings. Existing training budgets and metrics remain stated as before; the protocol behind revised Tanks and Temples scores is not fully established.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 adds confidence-map localization comparisons in B.3 and controlled corruption of smooth-region normal priors in B.4. B.1 adds training curves and rendering-weight profiles to investigate convergence under partial versus uniform unbiasing. These directly examine robustness and mechanisms previously supported mainly by ordinary reconstruction results and component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability bars, or statistical significance tests. The new inverse-variance curves and uncertainty-map comparisons concern model quantities, not statistical uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces ND-SDF's Tanks and Temples mean F-score of 9.35 with 14.46, while Table 4 changes MonoSDF's Replica F-score from 86.18 to 85.91. These are reported-value revisions, not established same-setting improvements. Added DebSDF results change some metric rankings. New Table 10 reports ND-SDF F-scores of 0.750 at zero bias and 0.655 at 60 degrees, alongside additional qualitative and convergence findings.

T1.justification: Equation 3 corrects the sign domains of the piecewise density formula: the first exponential branch changes from s(x) <= 0 to s(x) >= 0, and the second from s(x) > 0 to s(x) < 0. This fixes a mathematical inconsistency with the stated Laplace CDF. The remaining derivations and formal assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about normal deflection, adaptive prior supervision, guided optimization, and recovery of detailed indoor geometry. The additional experiments support these existing contributions rather than introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of geometric localization, robustness when smooth-region priors are wrong, and the relationship between inverse variance and surface sharpness. Appendix C.4 adds discussion of unbiasing failures and limitations of delaying unbiasing. Section 4.1 also replaces ScanNet++ superiority 'across all metrics' with a recall-focused interpretation. The original coverage and prior-dependence limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Grid/MLP comparator representations, explicitly locates the main ablations on ScanNet++, and documents SAM masking and normal rotation for the new robustness test. Conversely, Table 2 drops its explicit resolution of 768; the appendix specifies 2048 for qualitative comparisons only. Core implementation details, hardware, training time, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.4 acknowledges NC-SDF's similar SO(3) residual-field idea and argues differences in training, boundary information, and generalization, materially expanding positioning against a close concurrent approach. It also expands comparisons with NeuS, TUVR, and DebSDF. References for edge-aware reconstruction, edge detection, and Lang Segment Anything are added; DataP-SfM and FedSurfGS are removed. NC-SDF is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: The main exposition and section order remain largely intact. Changes include targeted wording and notation edits, more precise appendix references, acknowledgments, and the conference header. New appendix subsections and an expanded C.4 extend the narrative without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the existing paper.

P2.justification: v3 adds diagnostic Figures 11–13, qualitative comparison Figures 16–17, and robustness Table 10. Figure 4 and the Tanks and Temples comparison are replaced, and several benchmark tables gain comparator rows. Figure 2 relabels depth and normals as priors rather than ground truth. Earlier Replica and extraction-resolution figures are retained and relocated, not newly added results.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of how ND-SDF handles unreliable priors: it adds DebSDF comparisons across additional benchmarks, directly tests corrupted smooth-region priors, and supplies localization and convergence diagnostics absent from v2. Equation 3 and the ScanNet++ interpretation become more accurate. The robustness test remains limited to one scene, and revised Tanks and Temples scores lack a clear protocol explanation, but the added evidence substantially reduces important gaps in support for the central mechanism.
